gloss: to sprout; to bud; to emerge

definitions.explanation: When a plant begins to grow and produces its first shoots.
Figuratively, when feelings, ideas, or consciousness begin to develop.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になって、{新|あたら}しい{芽|め}が{芽生|めば}えてきた。
examples.english: Spring came and new buds began to sprout.

examples.japanese: {種|たね}をまいて{三日|みっか}で{芽|め}が{芽生|めば}えた。
examples.english: The seeds sprouted three days after sowing.

examples.japanese: {暖|あたた}かくなると、{庭|にわ}のあちこちで{草|くさ}が{芽生|めば}え{始|はじ}める。
examples.english: When it gets warm, grass starts sprouting here and there in the garden.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{間|あいだ}に{愛情|あいじょう}が{芽生|めば}えた。
examples.english: Love began to emerge between the two of them.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{心|こころ}に{正義|せいぎ}{感|かん}が{芽生|めば}え{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: A sense of justice began to emerge in the child's heart.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{旅行|りょこう}をきっかけに、{異文化|いぶんか}への{興味|きょうみ}が{芽生|めば}えた。
examples.english: Traveling abroad sparked an emerging interest in other cultures.

notes:
{芽生|めば}える is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}). There is no transitive pair.

ASPECT ({ている}):
{芽生|めば}えている indicates an ongoing process of sprouting or emerging.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {芽|め}が{芽生|めば}える - buds sprout
- {愛情|あいじょう}が{芽生|めば}える - love emerges
- {興味|きょうみ}が{芽生|めば}える - interest develops
- {意識|いしき}が{芽生|めば}える - awareness emerges
- {希望|きぼう}が{芽生|めば}える - hope arises

NOTE:
This verb is commonly used figuratively to describe the early development of emotions, ideas, or consciousness. It carries a positive, hopeful connotation of new beginnings.
